most_recent.text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Western Digital simply stopped working. A search of my options revealed that a 1TB Seagate may be a good choice. Despite the tracking history reading more like an unfinished novel, the plot improved after what seemed to be multiple, extra days. Seagate on a Mac is sadly NOT a plug-and-play; rather, it took reformatting and made my Time Machine much less useful. I had hoped to leave it connected to the MBA for auto back-ups but I find myself removing the laptop from its charging station so often that the current set-up makes little sense. My hope is to put the Time Machine back to work on daily back-ups and to perform manual back-ups via the Seagate once a week. All in all, the price point seems fair... I just hope Seagate gives me what I paid for.
most_recent.title: Goodbye Western Digital, Hello Seagate

most_recent.text: Part Number 2N1AP5-500, 2 Terrabyte model. Lived behind my computer for the past 3½ years. Just because I needed some more drive space. It served well in that format until yesterday. I was actively managing some files when all of a sudden, USB disconnect sound. No, it didn't come unplugged. But it was no longer talking to the computer and, the computer did not like the sudden hotswap while I was actively putting things on it... I had to force a shutdown and reboot, to find the whole computer being draggy. Windows troubleshooting and waiting until today, only then I found out it was this drive being a boat anchor for the whole system. Actively freezes programs, key ones too like file manager and task manager. The drive will no longer read or write. Just emits a monotonous clicking in rithym, obviously the reader going back and forth in a trance. I never really touched this on regular occasion, it just lived behind the computer, quietly holding files until that failiure happened. I don't know if the cable failed, or if the drive itself is dead. But if you're keeping stuff on this important, better copy it to another drive because it seems it may just decide to lock itself in its room like a pouting teenager. No more talking, your files are mine forever. The second I unplug the drive the computer jumps back to life. This drive, singlehandedly, crippled the entire OS. And it didn't even have any OS related software on it. So now im out a drive because my computer has abysmal internal capacity, and I'll probably have to pay a technician to go perform an autopsy on this drive to try and see if the disk in it is recoverable and transplantable. So I now have a rectangular slab of landwaste and a cable with a proprietary connector I can't use anywhere else... how is your day going then?
most_recent.title: Sudden Sweet Death
